A kernel-based root solution for Android

Starts CVeyra\'s persistent shell broker. Wireless ADB is used to bootstrap the shell identity, then CVeyra keeps its own authenticated local broker outside the app process. Root remains optional through the separate Root switch.

resources.string: Reads the kernel symbol table out of a boot.img, resolves the offsets this exploit chain needs, and rewrites the chosen base library into a build that matches your kernel. Tapping "Build payload" asks which scheme to use first: the universal one covers most devices, while vivo / iQOO needs the build carrying the vr.ko anti-root bypass. Everything happens on-device — no network.

Only the parts that are needed are fetched — the ZIP central directory, the payload manifest, and the few tens of MiB the boot partition occupies — not the whole package (usually 4–8 GiB).\nThe server must support HTTP Range requests; if it does not, the request is refused rather than silently downloading everything.

CVeyra keeps every app on its normal Android UID and brokers privileged actions through a visible, per-app policy layer. With CVeyra Access active, the broker is enforced through VeyraKSU and Veyra’s root backend.
Activation requires VeyraKSU 2.0.0 and a KernelSU Superuser grant for Veyra. The existing KernelSU app-grant state is backed up before the full permission manager is enforced.

Offline keeps rules stored without managing apps. Self lets you choose apps yourself. Auto is reserved for a later policy engine and is not enabled yet. Detailed per-app privileges remain visible on Grant CVeyra Access.

Older direct KernelSU grants remain KernelSU-managed and are backed up before CVeyra Access is accepted. Veyra does not silently delete them; add those apps to CVeyra when you want to migrate their management.

CVeyra modules can temporarily change real device settings such as Accessibility, Developer options, USB debugging or Private DNS. The exact previous values are saved and restored when the module is disabled.

The firewall combines Android’s package networking gate with a root-persistent IPv4/IPv6 UID rule layer. Veyra remembers only the apps it manages and reapplies its own rules after the VeyraKSU module starts.
